history.content: What happens in a T Tauri phase?

In the T Tauri phase, a star is surrounded by a dense disk of gas and dust. The star ejects extremely hot winds dominated by positively charged particles called protons and neutral helium atoms. While some of the material from the disk is still falling onto the star, small groups of dust particles are colliding and clumping together, growing into larger objects. These are the building blocks of planets, sometimes called "planetesimals."

What is the precise composition and distribution of elements within the dust and gas disks of different types of stars during their T Tauri phase, and how does this variation affect the formation of planets around these stars?
